title: MySQL Architecture Overview knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “MySQL Architecture Overview”?
options: It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.

A client sends a statement to the MySQL server; the server parses and optimizes it, executes it through the relevant storage engine, and returns a result or status. Persistent storage and transaction rules govern what survives.
It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
questions.answer_key: A client sends a statement to the MySQL server; the server parses and optimizes it, executes it through the relevant storage engine, and returns a result or status. Persistent storage and transaction rules govern what survives.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: A client sends a statement to the MySQL server; the server parses and optimizes it, executes it through the relevant storage engine, and returns a result or status. Persistent storage and transaction rules govern what survives.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “MySQL Architecture Overview” safely?
options: Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Apply MySQL Architecture Overview to a synthetic MySQL lab scenario, write down the expected outcome, and specify how you will verify it safely.
Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
questions.answer_key: Apply MySQL Architecture Overview to a synthetic MySQL lab scenario, write down the expected outcome, and specify how you will verify it safely.
questions.explanation: Apply MySQL Architecture Overview to a synthetic MySQL lab scenario, write down the expected outcome, and specify how you will verify it safely. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “MySQL Architecture Overview”, what should be verified?

Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
